subject: DPIA & Art.28/30 extracts for proposed model fine-tune - access & timeline

Subject: DPIA support + Art.28/30 extracts for fine-tune project

Hi Vanessa,

Kestrel is moving forward with a pilot to fine-tune an open model on de-identified patient records for clinical summarization. Our legal and privacy teams have asked for the following before we can sign off:

- A short DPIA scoping form that shows how Redwood will process trainer data for fine-tuning (controls, retention, deletion).
- Export of an Art.30 processing register excerpt covering the inference and any model-training subprocessors (we only need the rows relevant to the pilot).
- Confirmation of where fine-tuning compute will run (onshore-only requirement).
- Timeboxed auditor access (TrustAssure) to a read-only evidence bundle containing logs, Art.28 subprocessors list, and sampling of retention artifacts.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can support this and share an expected timeline? We are aiming to start the pilot the week of Aug 17 and need evidence to satisfy our internal DPA queue by Aug 13.

If it helps, I can loop in our auditor (audit contact is auditor@trustassure.com).

Thanks,
Sara

Hi all — looping in privacy/ops details. Helpful to confirm the items Vanessa mentioned. A few operational notes we will deliver with the Art.30 excerpt and DPIA scoping form: 

- Art.30 extract: CSV with processing activity rows filtered to Kestrel-related projects (we will redact unrelated account IDs). See attached sample (Art30_Register_Excerpt.csv).
- DPIA scoping form: short form to capture categories of data, legal basis, automated profiling, and intended safeguards (attached: DPIA_Scoping_Form.pdf).
- Subprocessor list: we will provide the active subprocessors relevant to training (infra, metrics, logging). Any subprocessors used for checkpoint storage will be explicitly flagged.
- Evidence access: we support two options — (A) a one-time evidence bundle delivered as a secure download, or (B) temporary SAML-backed portal access for TrustAssure limited to a 72-hour window. Option B is preferred for sensitive logs.

Operational constraints to call out: we do not export raw training inputs outside the region unless explicitly authorized in the DPA addendum. For model checkpoint persistence, we usually keep ephemeral checkpoints for up to 72 hours by default; if Kestrel needs a shorter window (e.g., 0 hours), we can update runtime config for the pilot.

Next steps I suggest:
- Kestrel to confirm: dataset delivery model (upload to Redwood staging, or run in Kestrel VPC).
- Confirm auditor access preference (download vs portal + SAML).
- Sign the DPA addendum (DPA_Redline_v2.docx) or propose redlines.

I can take the lead on assembling the Art.30 extract and the evidence bundle once we have those clarifications.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Privacy Program Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Thanks Vanessa and Marissa — quick answers and preferences:

- Kestrel will upload a de-identified dataset to Redwood staging (S3 presigned) for the pilot; we will not use Kestrel VPC for the initial run.
- Retention: we need no longer than 24 hours for intermediate artifacts and zero retention for model checkpoints post-training (delete on job completion).
- Auditor access: TrustAssure prefers temporary portal access (SAML) for a 48-hour window. Auditor contact is auditor@trustassure.com.

We can sign a targeted addendum to the DPA. The Aug 13 deadline is firm — our procurement/legal teams need artifacts attached to the onboarding ticket by then.

Can you confirm whether Redwood will support checkpoint auto-delete on job completion? Also, please provide the portal SAML SP metadata and the expected date/time window you can provision access.

Thanks,
Sara
